config.dataset: Northwind — 10k customers, 200 employees, 1k suppliers, 5k products, 50k orders, 308,224 order_details
config.driver: pg (node-postgres) pool max:12, identical across ORMs
config.load: k6 ramping-VUs 0→200→400 (~25s), full 13-route requests.json replay (426,999 requests)
config.machine: single local dev box, Node 26.8.1 (server + k6 co-located)
config.note: Unlike the upstream 2-machine / 3000-VU rig, this is a single-box short-ramp run — treat relative ordering as indicative, absolute numbers as low. p50 omitted (k6 --summary-export does not emit it); avg/p90/p95 are the measured percentiles.

prepared.note: Head-to-head: same zmdb server with ZMDB_PREPARED=1 (server-side prepared statements — stable statement name per compiled SQL, so Postgres caches the plan). Reproducible across 2 runs.
prepared.verdict: ZMDB_PREPARED=1 reproducibly improves zmdb: +4–5% req/s, −3–4% avg, ~−11ms p90, ~−9–14ms p95. The tail-latency lever works — kept opt-in to preserve the zero-state default.
